  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,

  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,

  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there

  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 850 9072 2911, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 27, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  ARMENIAN GENOCIDE REMEMBERANCE

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN presented a proclamation declaring April 24, 2021 as a day of
remembrance of the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1923. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN
stated that this year the President of the United States formally recognized the Armenian
Genocide, which followed recognition by both Houses of the US Congress in 2019. MAYOR
PRO TEM ZERUNYAN shared how his family was affected by the Armenian Genocide and
expressed the importance of having the legal and moral authority to speak out about crimes
against humanity so that they do not happen again.

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  PVPUSD UPDATE FROM SUPERINTENDENT DR. CHERNISS

  Superintendent Cherniss and Board Member Crawford provided an update regarding
  school openings, announcing that all schools are back to in-person instruction four days
  a week. He added that remote learning will continue for those who prefer learning in an
  online environment. Programs to help children with challenges were discussed. Board
  Member Crawford added that due to the recent unforeseen vacancy on the School
  Board, the Board voted to appoint someone to fill the vacant spot through 2022.

  Discussion ensued on how to apply, the target date for the new member to be installed
  as well as what resources are available to help the students who face mental health
  challenges due to the COVID-19 epidemic.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 27, 2021
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-I AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

  REPORT.

Discussion ensued regarding City-operated dog water stations and how they have been
maintained during the COVID-19 epidemic.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Linus Yeh, Kick Ash Coalition member provided a verbal invitation to the upcoming Town
Hall Q&A panel of experts including RHE Mayor Zuckerman.

Lisa Van Ingen Pope, Parks & Activities Commission Chair shared that the Commission
recently met for the first time in over a year at their annual park tour at George F Canyon;
noting she will have more to report in the coming months.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 27, 2021
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A  SECOND AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING -
  COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING PROGRAM

Kathleen McGowan of McGowan Consulting provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Discussion ensued regarding permitting requirements, anticipated reduction in flow volumes
and anticipated cost savings.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN TO
  APPROVE AND AUTHORIZE EXECUTION OF THE SECOND AMENDMENT
  TO THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, THE COUNTY OF LOS
  ANGELES, AND THE CITIES OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES, PALOS
  VERDES ESTATES, ROLLING HILLS AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  REGARDING THE ADMINISTRATION AND COST SHARING FOR
  IMPLEMENTING THE COORDINATED INTEGRATED MONITORING
  PROGRAM (CIMP) FOR THE PENINSULA CIMP AGENCIES.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO SB 210

Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ TO APPROVE AND AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE
  LETTER INCLUDED IN ATTACHMENT A

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  GOGOV MOBILE APPLICATION UPDATEREPORT

Administrative Aide Levi Sinkler provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued and concern was noted regarding contract automatic renewal and how to
budget for future price increase.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA voiced concern over the limited use of the app by residents,
pointing out that only 500 Rancho Palos Verdes residents have currently signed up to use it.
Additionally, she noted not seeing this address the concern of reaching staff afterhours in the
event of an emergency.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 27, 2021
 Public Comment:

Lyneigh Palacios, RHE resident, voiced support for the app as a trial to assist staff in
addressing issues in a timely manner.

Discussion ensued on how this app can be used to assist staff with resident follow by way of
implementing an additional workflow process, to better help manage follow up through
resolution.
  COUNCIL consensus for staff to return to Council with additional information.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 734 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 8.12 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO PUBLIC NUISANCES

City Attorney Don Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
ADOPT AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
ESTATES, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 8.12 (PUBLIC
NUISANCES) OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE AND MAKING
CONFORMING AMENDMENTS TO CHAPTER 1.24

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported the Equestrian Committee reviewed fees at its last
meeting and recommended no changes at this time.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that many COVID-19 restrictions having been relaxed, which
will allow for horse shows to resume.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that the trainer business list update is now posted on the
website. She added that there are 18 regular trainers using the facilities.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF announced that upcoming events remain postponed including the
Mayor’s Breakfast Ride and the Tracy Austin Tennis Tournament.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also noted that she attended the Palos Verdes Chamber of
Commerce Economic Committee meeting where staff reviewed the results of their business
survey, and she added that SB 93 signed by the Governor will present a hardship on the
Terranea Resort.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported that she attended her first League of California Cities
Transportation, Communications and Public Works Policy Committee Meeting and shared
the Committee’s action item to support AB 1060 the California Emergency Services Act, for a
statewide emergency alert system called California Alert.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported the Palos Verdes Peninsula Transit Authority met and
decided to purchase new clean fuel buses cleaner.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 27, 2021
 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN advised residents to fully screen their homes and to remove standing
water to address concerns about mosquitos.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN stated that the Vector Control District hired a new Executive Director
but that the former Director will stay on for a limited time to provide support to the new Director.

City Manager Grammer reported that the CDC announced that fully vaccinated people are no
longer required to wear masks in outdoor settings unless in a large crowd. He added that Los
Angeles County has met the requirements for the Yellow Tier and if it continues through next
week, there will be a further easing of restrictions and capacity limits.. Additionally, City
Manager Grammer reported that the County added a new vaccine tracker on the Public Health
website that lists vaccination rates for the County and each city within the County. He noted
the County vaccination rate for those16 years old and older is 48% and the RHE rate is 69%;
additionally, within the 65 and older age category, the County rate is almost 75% and RHE is
90%.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

15.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:11 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regularly
scheduled meeting to be held on Tuesday, May 11, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
Interim City Clerk  Mayor
